libs.note: BH-8314. The page half of request_human() in the web-task lane: on the run's site only, it holds the run's page open while wh_request_human waits for a person, types the code the person sends into that page, and on no answer saves a resume record (step id, URL, the page's storage state) so a later run can resume with wh_resume_human. Slice C1 of #8314 applies it with lib_env_apply web-human-step in the web-task lane.

knobs.note: How long the human step waits for the page to load after it submits the code (or after an approval). Past it the step answers `error: human step timed out after <n>s`. The wait for the person is not this knob: it is the settings row web_task.human_wait_s. A value that is not an integer in 5..120 makes createHumanStep throw; it is never clamped. Read by createHumanStep as env WEB_TASK_HUMAN_STEP_TIMEOUT_S, fallback 20.

How long a resume record (<state dir>/<step>.json and <step>.storage.json) stays on disk. Each save deletes the records saved before this window. The default is the top of the web_task.human_answer_ttl_s bounds (7 days), so no step that can still be answered loses its record. A value that is not an integer in 3600..604800 makes createHumanStep throw; it is never clamped. Read by createHumanStep as env WEB_TASK_HUMAN_RESUME_KEEP_S, fallback 604800.
